answer:
The Transformer computes attention as "Scaled Dot-Product Attention": it maps a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output via Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V — the dot products of each query with all keys are scaled by 1/√d_k (to keep softmax gradients healthy for large d_k), softmaxed into weights, and used to form a weighted sum of the values (arXiv:1706.03762v7, §3.2.1). Multi-Head Attention instead runs h = 8 parallel attention layers on h learned linear projections of Q/K/V (d_k = d_v = 64 = 512/8), concatenating and projecting the results so the model can jointly attend to different representation subspaces that a single averaging head would blur (§3.2.2). These attention sub-layers are stacked (N = 6 layers each) with position-wise feed-forward networks, residual connections, and layer normalization; the decoder additionally masks self-attention to future positions and attends over the encoder output (§3.1, §3.2.3), and since the model has no recurrence or convolution, sinusoidal positional encodings are added to inject token order (§3.5).

It replaces recurrence and convolution because: (1) recurrence is inherently sequential — hidden state h_t depends on h_{t−1} — precluding parallelization within training examples, while a self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations versus O(n) for a recurrent layer (§1, §4); (2) it shortens learning of long-range dependencies — the path between any two positions is O(1), versus O(n) for RNNs and paths that grow with distance for ConvS2S/ByteNet, which make distant dependencies harder to learn (§2, §4); (3) connecting all position pairs with convolutions requires a stack of O(n/k) layers (or O(log_k n) dilated), making convolutional layers generally more expensive than recurrent ones by a factor of k (§4); and (4) per-layer complexity is lower than recurrence when sequence length n < representation dimension d, which holds for typical machine-translation representations, and dot-product attention is fast and space-efficient because it uses optimized matrix multiplication (§3.2.1, §4). Empirically this yields superior translation quality while being more parallelizable and far cheaper to train (Abstract, §6.1).

Sources: Vaswani et al., "Attention Is All You Need," arXiv:1706.03762v7 (HTML full text, https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7 — §1 Introduction, §2 Background, §3.1–3.5, §4 "Why Self-Attention," Abstract).
